title: Gang scheduling latency clustering & LDMA timeline (Nsight session notes)
body:
Purpose:
Quick notes from an ad-hoc Nsight session focusing on an intermittent tail-latency spike we saw on the 8xA100 serving cluster when microbatching concurrent small inferences. Primary hypothesis: gang scheduling interactions + LDMA (L2/L3 DMA) contention cause kernel launch clustering and gaps in active SMs, which increases token-steering stalls and KV-cache rebuilds.

Context / why this matters:
- Observed 95th/99th token latency regressions on small payloads (<=64 tokens) across mixed workloads.
- Correlated with a higher ratio of small concurrent requests after we rolled canary for route /chat/fast.
- Production config: microbatching enabled, continuous KV caching, cuda-graph warmup on first request.

Testbed / reproducibility:
- Node: g4dn-ish, but tests run on internal 8xA100-p4d (nvlink enabled).
- Runtime: rwi-runtime v2.13.1 (branch: perf/gang-nsight).
- Model: llama-13b-quantized (kvm enabled), seq_len config: [1..64].
- Workload generator: local loadgen with poisson arrivals, concurrency sweep 4..64, payload size 8/32/64.

Commands / capture recipe:
- Start Nsight Systems with fine timeline + kernel correlation: nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none -o nsight/gang-ldma-run1 nsys_profile_wrapper.sh
- Export timeline: ncu-ui --import nsight/gang-ldma-run1.qdrep then File -> Export -> CSV timeline
- Capture per-kernel occupancy: nvprof (light) run to gather occupancy counters: nvprof --metrics sm_efficiency,achieved_occupancy ./rwi_bench --mode microbatch
- CUDA Graph trace: enable graph replay logging (RWI env var: RWI_GRAPH_DEBUG=1) and store launch timestamps to /tmp/graph-trace.log

High level observations (from Nsight timeline):
- Kernel launches are strongly clustered into 2 phases per request: a small setup kernel (prepack / KV-prefetch) followed by the main decode kernels.
- When concurrency >= 24, clusters from different requests begin to align, causing transient L2 bandwidth spikes (LDMA bursts) visible as busier NvLink traffic and longer memcpy peaks to device global memory.
- Between clustered bursts there are gaps where SM utilization drops to 6-12% for ~700-1200us, even though the process has in-flight work queued.
- These gaps line up with CUDA graph replay points in many cases; graph replay serialization appears to block async-copy streams briefly while the graph host replay kicks in.
- Some batches show prefetch kernels running on higher-priority streams while decode kernels are queued on default streams; stream priority inversion visible in timeline (see notes below).

Counter examples / when problem does NOT appear:
- Large seq_len workloads (>=1024) fully saturate SMs and gaps disappear.
- Tests on single-tenant fixed-throughput pools (dedicated capacity) show fewer LDMA spikes — suggests multi-tenant scheduling / gang-scheduling on the node is a factor.

Detailed timeline notes (excerpts):
- 00:00:02.143: request A prefetch kernel (stream 3, low prio) -> memcpy async H2D (LDMA channel 1) ~180us
- 00:00:02.328: request B prefetch kernel (stream 3) -> memcpy async H2D (LDMA channel 2) ~190us
- 00:00:02.520: graph-replay host call (thread X) -> cudaGraphLaunch -> host-side graph replay serialization ~420us
- 00:00:02.940: main decode kernel queued (stream 0) but waits ~680us before scheduling, SM util drops to 9%
- 00:00:03.630: sequence of smaller kernels (attention slice kernels) execute in quick succession, SM util spikes to 82% for 60us then drops

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Graph replay causes short host-side serialization that pauses async-copy progressors (LDMA), jointly causing kernel queuing behind memcpy and creating apparent SM idle gaps.
2) LDMA channel saturation from overlapping prefetches across tenants / contexts increases memcpy tail latency which delays decode kernels.
3) Stream priority mismatch (prefetch low prio, decode default prio) combined with OS-level gang scheduling causes prefetches to steal DMA time while decode waits for SMs.
4) NVLINK congestion and L2 thrash amplify the above under mixed model sizes when KV-cache warms.

Quick experiments to validate (done / planned):
- Disable cuda-graph replay for a subset of workers: observed 40% reduction in 99th token latency in a short A/B test (canary). (Executed 2024-12-05 by Marcelo O.)
- Force prefetches onto same stream as decode (co-streaming) to avoid cross-stream priority inversion. Early lab run reduced SM idle gaps but introduced occasional longer memcpy stalls. (Executed 2024-12-12 by Priya D.)
- Add jitter to prefetch start times (random 0..200us) to reduce synchronized LDMA bursts — small improvement on 95th latency. (Planned)
- Limit concurrent H2D async copies per GPU (throttle LDMA channels) via resource manager to test effect. (Planned, ticket RWI-3414)

Metrics / numbers observed:
- Baseline (no graph) 99th token latency: 18.4ms; with graph+multi-tenant: 28.9ms; with graph disabled on canary: 19.6ms
- SM util during steady decode (large seq): 85-92%
- SM util during regressed scenario: avg 32%, with idle gaps at 6-12% for 0.7-1.2ms windows

Action items and owners:
- (Aisha) Add detailed event logging around cudaGraphLaunch and graph replay start/end times to correlate host-side blocking (PR in runtime: perf/gang-graph-logs). Deadline: 2025-01-12.
- (Marcelo) Run LDMA-throttle experiments on staging. Capture Nsight traces for the same window lengths. Deadline: 2025-01-20.
- (Priya) Prototype co-streaming variant and run 72h soak on canary pool. Report regressions. Deadline: 2025-02-02.
- (Evan) Add resource-manager knob to limit concurrent H2D async copies per GPU and expose metric in Console. Deadline: 2025-02-10.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the graph replay path blocking one of the async-copy progress threads (driver-level) or is the runtime doing a blocking synchronization? Need driver-level logs.
- Does NVLink arbitration prefer certain L2 channels that interact badly when tenants overlap? Can we change prefetch spacing or prioritize decode copy lanes?

Notes / heuristics for next Nsight run:
- Capture both host and device timelines with thread names mapped to runtime components.
- Enable driver-level logging (cudaSetLogLevel) around graph replay.
- Re-run with single-tenant vs multi-tenant to isolate gang-scheduler effects.

References & pointers:
- Linear ticket: RWI-3414 (gang sched tail latency).
- GH: runtime PR perf/gang-graph-logs (WIP).
- Confluence: perf-inference/gpu-timeline-playbooks (internal).
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime perf -> message link (see Confluence page for transcript).

Raw artifacts location:
- nsight captures (zips) stored on s3://rwi-profiles/2024-11/gang-ldma/
- graph traces: /tmp/graph-trace-20241122.log (on test nodes)

Summary (short):
Current signals point to an interaction between cuda-graph replay host-side serialization and LDMA bursting from nearly-synchronous prefetches across concurrent requests. This creates small but repeated SM idle windows that blow up 99th token latency for small payload microbatched workloads. Early mitigation (disable graph on canary) shows meaningful improvement; next steps are targeted experiments (throttle LDMA, co-stream prefetching, add jitter) and better tracing to confirm driver vs runtime blocking.

Appendix: quick scratch commands and flags
- RWI_GRAPH_DEBUG=1 RWI_STREAM_PRIORITIZE_PREFETCH=1 RWI_PREFETCH_JITTER_US=100 ./rwi_bench --workers 32 --seq-len 32
- nsys profile -t cuda,nvtx,sm --sample=none -o /tmp/nsight/gang-ldma-run1 ./rwi_bench --trace-host
- nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency --csv -o /tmp/nvprof/occupancy.csv ./rwi_bench

-- End of notes --
